HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Geospace Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: GEOS) (“the “Company") today reported revenue for the fourth quarter ended September 30, 2026, of $19.6 million compared to revenue of $30.7 million for the comparable year-ago period. Net loss for the fourth quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $13.7 million, or $(1.06) per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $9.1 million, or $(0.71) per basic and diluted share, for the comparable year-ago period. The fourth quarter loss included non-cash charges of $3.5 million cumulative translation loss related to the Company’s Colombian operations and $2.9 million for underutilized assets related to select nodal rental tools and manufacturing equipment.

For the twelve-month period ended September 30, 2026, Geospace Technologies reported revenue of $80.7 million for its fiscal year ended September 30, 2026. This compares to revenue of $110.8 million for the comparable year-ago period. Net loss for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 was $44.3 million, or $(3.43) basic and per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $9.7 million, or $(0.76) per basic and diluted share, for comparable year-ago period.

Management’s Comments

Richard “Rich” Kelley, Chief Executive Officer and President of Geospace Technologies, said, “To provide an understanding of our financial performance this fiscal year, it is beneficial to consider the global economic picture. The year remained plagued by uncertainty and delays driven by ongoing changes in trade policy, a major Middle East energy disruption, continued sanctions, and shifts in borrowing costs. These significant factors negatively impacted our ability to conduct business in our current structure.

As such, the management team has taken decisive steps to realign our operations, reduce costs, and position Geospace for a return to profitability. During fiscal year 2026, we have executed two reductions in force, an early retirement program, and cutbacks in expenses. Additionally, the challenging business conditions during fiscal 2026 contributed to non-cash charges recorded for the fiscal year of approximately $6 million of cumulative foreign exchange loss and underutilized equipment.

Our Smart Water segment experienced disappointing declines driven predominantly by decreases in orders for our Hydroconn line of smart water meter connector cables. Evaluation of broader market conditions point to slower hardware shipments, uneven project deployments, and normalization following earlier demand surges. Several major metering suppliers are experiencing near-term hardware and deployment softness, while longer-term modernization demand appears more resilient. As part of our business restructuring, we concluded a decades long relationship with an external manufacturing representative firm, who exclusively marketed the Hydroconn connectors. In fiscal year 2027, we will use internal sales and marketing resources to build demand and secure specifications of our products in utility AMI-related procurements. This approach will reduce expenses associated with representative commissions and increase our control over product promotion and increase customer intimacy. While the contribution from the Aquana brand remains modest, the products continue to grow with 51% year over year revenue increases. In the coming year, we look to build upon the growth in Aquana revenue and maximize our early efforts with white label product manufacturing to support a revenue rebound in this segment.

Our Energy Solutions segment experienced the impacts of energy market volatility and project timing shifts, increased component and shipping costs, as well as access to raw materials. Increased competition and consolidation remain challenging in the marine exploration market and have led to decreased demand for our ocean-bottom nodes. The segment focused resources on execution of sizable contracts including the Petrobras Permanent Reservoir Monitoring (PRM) program, which is expected to be shipped and product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027. The previously cited global conditions proved harshest for our energy sales efforts, however, we have a strong backlog in this segment going into the next fiscal year. Long-term demand forecasts should drive more favorable land exploration market conditions resulting in additional Pioneer contracts.

For the Intelligent Industrial segment, the economic headwinds were less severe but still influenced revenue timing. The biggest factor impacting revenue generation was government procurement timing at state and federal levels. After a lengthy effort, our Quantum Technology Sciences subsidiary entered into a $10.8 million contract with the U.S. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane Division, Crane, Indiana for the Company’s Seismic Acoustic Detection and Ranging Underwater System. Similar timing delays have occurred around the sale of the Heartbeat Detector®, a vehicle security screening technology used by correctional and border agencies. Lengthy procurement cycles and complex approvals have resulted in slower than expected revenue recognition with this product line, but the outlook and demand for the technology remain extremely encouraging.

Despite this incredibly challenging year, our restructuring decisions and implementation will set the company more solidly on a return to profitability in fiscal year 2027. We concluded fiscal year 2026 with a backlog exceeding $100 million from contracts across our three segments. Contributions to the backlog encompass not only the PRM program, but contracts with the U.S. Federal government and other agencies as well as contract manufacturing customers and smart water white label commitments. The strong backlog, a well targeted acquisition strategy and restructured operations prepare Geospace well for the future.”

Smart Water Segment

Revenue from the Company’s Smart Water segment totaled $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $8.5 million in revenue for the same period a year ago a decrease of 63%. For the fiscal year, revenue from this segment totaled $17.2 million versus $35.8 million for the same prior year period for a decrease of 52%. The decrease in revenue for the three-month and twelve-month periods is due to decreased demand for our Hydroconn universal AMI connectors.

Energy Solutions Segment

For the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, revenue from the Company’s Energy Solutions segment totaled $10.8 million for a decrease of 31% when compared to $15.7 million from the same prior year period. Revenue from the twelve-month period was $40.9 million, a decrease of 19%, when compared to revenue from the same prior year period of $50.7 million. The decrease for the three-month period and twelve-month period is due to lower utilization and sales for our marine ocean bottom node rental fleet, partially offset by revenue recognized related to performance on our PRM contract and sales of the Company’s ultralight land node known as Pioneer.

Intelligent Industrial Segment

Revenue from the Company’s Intelligent Industrial segment totaled $5.6 million for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026. This compares with $6.4 million from the equivalent year ago period, representing a decrease of 12%. Revenue for the twelve-month period ending September 30, 2026, was $22.2 million. This compares to the prior year-ago period of $24.0 million, a decrease of 7%. The decrease in revenue for the three-month period and twelve-month period was due to lower demand for our industrial sensors, and imaging products, partially offset by an increase in security and defense revenue.

Balance Sheet and Liquidity

For the twelve-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Company used $35.1 million in cash and cash equivalents from operating activities. The Company generated $9.8 million of cash from investing activities that included $12.1 million of proceeds from the sale of rental equipment, $1.4 million in proceeds from the sale of property, plant and equipment and, offset by $3.9 million for additions to property, plant and equipment. The Company generated $7.1 million of cash from financing activities of which $7.5 million was from borrowings from the Company’s Woodforest credit facility.

On October 29, 2026, the Company entered into a Revolving Loan and Security Agreement with Amerisource Funding, Inc. (the "Amerisource Agreement"). The Company had a $7.5 million outstanding loan balance under the Woodforest Agreement, which was refinanced with borrowings under the Amerisource Agreement at closing. The Amerisource Agreement is for a three-year term and provides a revolving credit facility with a maximum availability of $25 million, subject to a borrowing base. Interest shall accrue on outstanding borrowings at the prime rate plus 3.5% per annum. The Company is required to make monthly interest payments on borrowed funds. The Amerisource Agreement is secured by substantially all of the Company’s assets, except for certain excluded property, and is guaranteed by certain of the Company’s subsidiaries. As of the date of this announcement, the Company has available borrowings of approximately $13 million.

Conference Call Information

Geospace Technologies will host a conference call to review its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026 financial results on Friday, November 20, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (9 a.m. Central). Participants can access the call at 833-316-1983 (US) or 785-838-9310 (International). Please reference the conference ID: GEOSQ426 prior to the start of the conference call. A replay will be available for approximately 60 days and may be accessed through the Investor Relations page of our website at www.geospace.com.

About Geospace Technologies

Geospace Technologies is a global technology and instrumentation manufacturer specializing in advanced sensing, IOT and highly ruggedized products, which serve smart water, energy exploration, industrial, government and commercial customers worldwide. The Company’s products blend engineering expertise with advanced analytic software to optimize energy exploration, enhance national and homeland security, empower water utility and property managers, and streamline electronic printing solutions. With more than four decades of excellence, the Company’s 390 employees across the world are dedicated to engineering and technical quality. Geospace is traded on the U.S. NASDAQ stock exchange under the ticker symbol GEOS. For more information, visit www.geospace.com.

Key Terms

cumulative translation lossfinancial
The accumulated change in value that arises when a company translates the financial statements of its foreign operations into the reporting (presentation) currency; exchange-rate movements create periodic translation gains or losses that are recorded each period and summed as the cumulative translation loss. It is a non-cash accounting adjustment that typically appears in equity (as part of accumulated other comprehensive income or loss) rather than in operating profit, and the accumulated amount may be reclassified into profit or loss if the foreign operation is sold or substantially liquidated.
permanent reservoir monitoringtechnical
Permanent reservoir monitoring is the long-term use of sensors and measurement systems placed at or near an underground oil, gas or fluid reservoir to continuously track pressure, temperature, flow and small seismic changes. For investors it matters because continuous, real-time data reduces uncertainty about how much can be recovered, helps operators optimize production and costs, and lowers environmental and operational risk — like putting the asset on a continuous health monitor to inform valuation and investment decisions.
revolving credit facilityfinancial
A revolving credit facility is a type of loan that a business can borrow from whenever it needs money, up to a set limit. It’s like having a credit card for companies—allowing them to borrow, pay back, and borrow again as needed, providing flexibility for managing cash flow or funding short-term expenses.
borrowing basefinancial
A borrowing base is the amount a lender will allow a company to borrow based on the value of assets the company offers as security, typically things like accounts receivable and inventory. It matters to investors because it sets a practical ceiling on short-term financing and influences a company’s liquidity and risk: if the borrowing base falls, the company may lose access to cash or be forced to sell assets, which can affect operations and share value.

The Reverse Stock Split will become effective at 12:01 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Company's common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "CODX" and will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Reverse Stock Split is intended to enable the Company to maintain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market, and to maintain sufficient authorized shares available for issuance to allow the Company to conduct equity financings as needed. The new CUSIP number for the Company's common stock following the Reverse Stock Split will be 189763 303.

At the Special Meeting of Stockholders held on November 13, 2026 (the "Special Meeting"), the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Company's Articles of Incorporation, as amended, to effect one or more reverse stock splits of the Company's issued and outstanding shares of common stock, on one or more occasions, at a ratio of not less than 1-for-2, with the cumulative effect of all such reverse stock splits not to exceed 1-for-750, such final ratio or ratios and the timing and number of any reverse stock splits to be determined by the Company's board of directors at any time within twelve months following the Special Meeting, without further approval or authorization of the stockholders. Additional information regarding the Reverse Stock Split approved by stockholders can be found in the Company's definitive proxy statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on October 26, 2026.

The Amendment provides that at the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, each 25 shares of the Company's issued and outstanding common stock will be automatically combined into one (1) validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable share of common stock, without effecting a change to the par value per share. The Reverse Stock Split will impact all shares of the Company's common stock outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, as well as the number of shares of common stock available for issuance under the Company's equity incentive plans. The Reverse Stock Split will not change the number of shares of capital stock authorized for issuance under our Articles of Incorporation. Based on the 13,044,465 shares of common stock currently outstanding, we expect approximately 521,779 shares of common stock to be issued and outstanding following the Reverse Stock Split.

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders who would otherwise be entitled to receive fractional shares as a result of the Reverse Stock Split will have those shares rounded up to the next whole share. Stockholders with shares in brokerage accounts should direct any questions concerning the reverse stock split to their broker; all other stockholders may direct questions to the Company's transfer agent, VStock Transfer, LLC.

Melville, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - As previously disclosed, on December 23, 2025, FONAR Corporation (NASDAQ: FONR) ("FONAR" or the "Company") entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with FONAR, LLC ("Parent") and Fonar Acquisition Sub, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), pursuant to which, subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, Parent would acquire the Company in an all-cash merger (the "Merger"). Under Section 3.22(a) of the Merger Agreement, the Merger was conditioned on (a) the affirmative vote of shares representing a majority of the stock outstanding and entitled to vote, voting together as a single class, after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock, and (b) the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast by disinterested stockholders, voting together as a single class after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock.

On February 2, 2026, plaintiff Bruce Taylor ("Plaintiff"), a purported stockholder of the Company, filed a Verified Stockholder Class Action Complaint (the "Complaint"), on behalf of himself and all other similarly situated stockholders of the Company, in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (the "Court"), captioned Taylor v. Fonar Corporation, et al., C.A. No. 2026-0142-JTL (the "Action"). The Complaint named as defendants the Company, Parent, Merger Sub, and Timothy Damadian, Luciano Bonanni, Robert M. Carrino, Ronald G. Lehman, and Richard E. Turk (the "Individual Defendants" and, together with the Company, Parent, and Merger Sub, the "Defendants").

The Complaint alleged that, under Section 203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law ("Section 203"), the Merger must be conditioned on the affirmative vote of at least 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder, as provided in Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Vote"). The Complaint further alleged that the Individual Defendants breached their fiduciary duties in connection with the foregoing.

Defendants have denied, and continue to deny, that they committed any violation of law or engaged in any of the wrongful acts that were or could have been alleged in the Action, and expressly maintain that they complied with their fiduciary and other legal duties.

On May 29, 2026, the Company filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a Current Report on Form 8-K calculating the Section 203 Vote, and the Company received approval of the requisite 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder under Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Approval").

On June 5, 2026, the Court granted and approved a stipulation and order voluntarily dismissing the Action as moot (the "Dismissal Order"). The Dismissal Order dismissed all claims in the Action with prejudice only as to Plaintiff and without prejudice as to any actual or potential claims of any other members of the putative class, and the Court retained jurisdiction to determine Plaintiff's application for an award of attorneys' fees and expenses (the "Fee and Expense Application"). The Dismissal Order was without prejudice to Plaintiff's ability to subsequently file claims challenging the fairness of the Merger and/or the adequacy of the Company's disclosures in connection with the Merger on any basis other than the adequacy of the Company's disclosures regarding Section 203, and Defendants reserved all rights with respect to any such claims.

Following arm's-length negotiations, the parties to the Action agreed to fully resolve the Fee and Expense Application through a payment to Plaintiff's counsel, which the Company will make and/or cause to be made on behalf of all Defendants, in the amount of $1,600,000 (the "Mootness Fee"). The Company, while denying any and all liability, agreed to the Mootness Fee in the exercise of its business judgment in order to avoid the cost, distraction, and uncertainty of further litigation regarding the Fee and Expense Application. The Court has not been asked to review and will not pass judgment on the payment of the Mootness Fee.

On November 15, 2026, the Court entered a Stipulation and Order Governing Plaintiff's Counsel's Award of Attorneys' Fees and Expenses, Notice of Mootness Fee and Closing the Action (the "Fee Order"). Pursuant to the Fee Order, within thirty (30) calendar days of the later of (i) the Court's entry of the Fee Order or (ii) the provision by Plaintiff's counsel of a Form W-9 and wiring instructions to the Company, the Company will pay or cause to be paid the Mootness Fee to Plaintiff's counsel in full and complete satisfaction of the Fee and Expense Application in connection with the Action. Upon receipt of such payment, Plaintiff and Plaintiff's counsel will be deemed to have fully and completely released all Defendants, and each of their respective subsidiaries, affiliates, parents, divisions, directors, officers, employees, predecessors and successors, managers, equity holders, beneficiaries, members, any related persons or entities, insurers, trustees, administrators, representatives and fiduciaries, successors, assigns and agents, from all claims for attorneys' fees and expenses in connection with the Action.

This Notice is being disseminated pursuant to the Fee Order and constitutes notice to the Company's stockholders, including the members of the putative class, to the extent required under Court of Chancery Rule 23. Pursuant to the Fee Order, within five (5) business days of the dissemination of this notice, the Company will file an affidavit with the Court confirming its compliance with the Fee Order's notice requirement, upon which the Register in Chancery is directed to close the Action on the docket for all purposes.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tenet Fintech Group Inc. (CSE: PKK) (OTCQB: PKKFF) (FSE: P0T) ("Tenet" or the "Company"), an innovative analytics service provider, owner and operator of the Cubeler Business Hub, today announced its financial results and operating highlights for the three-month and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Tenet reported revenue of $66,070,573 for the quarter, compared to $192,769 in the third quarter of 2025, and a net profit of $1,593,915 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 in the third quarter of 2025. All amounts in this news release are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Q3-2026 Key Financial Figures

  • Total Revenue of $66.07 million

  • Net Profit of $1.59 million

Q3-2026 Operating Highlights

The Company's value-added services to China's real estate development and construction sector supply chains through its GoldRiver and Cubeler Business Hub platforms continued to drive revenue in the third quarter of 2026 and provided a solid foundation to build on. Tenet's November 2025 breakthrough framework agreement with Chengdu Honglongyi Trading Ltd. ("CHTL") was the catalyst for much of the activity on the Company's platforms through the first three quarters of 2026. For most of the first half of 2026, CHTL was the sole customer driving meaningful supply-chain-related activity on the Company's platforms. To reduce its dependency on a single customer, the Company made increasing the number of its supply-chain customers a priority. The Company added five new customers between the latter part of the second quarter and the end of the third quarter, bringing the number of customers that contributed to its supply-chain-related revenue during the third quarter to a total of six, including CHTL.

Tenet officially ceased its operations in China's small-business commercial-lending space by selling its 51% ownership stake in its Asia Synergy Financial Capital ("ASFC") subsidiary during the third quarter of 2026. The transaction aligns with the Company's stated desire to focus its operations in China on data aggregation and supply-chain-related activities. The sale of ASFC not only frees up valuable resources but is expected to provide significant capital that can be allocated to bolster the Company's supply-chain-related activities and data-related service offerings in both China and North America.

Although the Company was still not at the commercialization phase during the third quarter of 2026 when it comes to its data-derived product offering, the Company believes that relevant progress was made toward achieving that objective. Tenet made several enhancements to the Cubeler Business Hub, including the addition of a grant-matching feature for registered members, to make the platform more enticing for SMEs. The Company also enhanced its offering to accountants and bookkeepers with the launch of its BKeeper platform allowing them to offer their SME clients with a host of AI-powered value-added services. Those initiatives, combined with the arrival of a new sales manager, contributed to a noticeable increase in the rate of SME registrations on the Cubeler Business Hub during the quarter. With the increase in the amount of SME data at its disposal during the quarter, the Company was optimistic that the launch of a commercially viable series of Canadian economic indexes could be achieved in relatively short order.

Q3-2026 Financial Results Summary

The Company's reported net income in Q3 was significantly impacted by certain nonrecurring events during the quarter. Those events include: 1) the profit realized on the sale of the Company's ASFC financial services subsidiary; 2) the commission paid related to the $225M minimum guaranteed annual revenue agreement signed with Sum Hung Hang Tai Trading Ltd.; 3) the grant of stock options to directors, officers, employees and consultants; 4) an increase in expected credit loss provision related to prepayments made to certain subcontractors dating back to 2022; and 5) the impairment of intangible assets related to ASFC. Together, these five events accounted for net expenses of a little more than $1.7M for the Company in the third quarter, which explains the lower net income reported for the quarter compared to the previous quarter, despite the quarter-over-quarter revenue increase from Q2-2026 to Q3-2026.

In summary, the Company generated revenue of $66,070,573 for the three-month period and $129,443,140 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to $192,769 for the three-month period and $736,677 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

Total expenses before taxes for the quarter amounted to $63,406,975 compared to $3,702,406 for the same period in 2025. The Company realized a net profit of $1,593,915 for the three-month period and $4,984,526 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 for the three-month period and a net loss of $9,156,663 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

Revised Full-Year 2026 Revenue Guidance

Tenet's strong third-quarter results, coupled with the addition of new clients for its supply-chain-related service offerings, led the Company to revise its full-year 2026 revenue guidance range to between $190 million and $195 million (up from $175 million to $180 million). Tenet expects gross profit margins of 9% to 11% and net income of $9.8 million to $10.5 million. The revised numbers should only marginally affect Tenet's previously forecasted EPS, which the Company has kept at $0.02 to $0.025 for fiscal year 2026.

The Trust was formed to own an overriding royalty interest of the net proceeds attributable to certain producing oil and gas properties located in the Hugoton field of Kansas and the San Juan Basin fields of New Mexico and Colorado. As described in the Trust's public filings, the amount of the monthly distributions is expected to fluctuate from month to month, depending on the proceeds, if any, received by the Trust as a result of production, oil and natural gas prices, and the amount of the Trust’s administrative expenses and reimbursements received from working interest owners, among other factors. In addition, as further described in the Trust’s most recent filing on Form 10-Q, distributions to unitholders are expected to be materially reduced, until the Trust increases its cash reserves to a total of $2.0 million in order to provide added liquidity.

Proceeds reported by the working interest owners for any month are not generally representative of net proceeds that will be received by the Trust in future periods. As further described in the Trust’s Form 10-K and Form 10-Q filings, production and development costs for the royalty interest have resulted in substantial accumulated excess production costs, which will decrease Trust distributions, and in some periods may result in no Trust distributions. The amount of proceeds, if any, received or expected to be received by the Trust (and its ability to pay distributions to unitholders) has been and will continue to be directly affected, among other things, by volatility in the industry and revenues and expenses reported to the Trust by working interest owners. Any additional expenses and adjustments, among other things, will reduce proceeds to the Trust, which will reduce the amount of cash available for distribution to unitholders and in certain periods could result in no distributions to unitholders.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For customers, electric reliability is measured in everyday moments: whether the lights come on in the morning, a business can keep its doors open and power is restored quickly when an outage occurs. For the 21st consecutive year, San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E), a subsidiary of Sempra (NYSE: SRE), has been recognized as the most reliable electric utility in the West. PA Consulting presented SDG&E with the 2026 ReliabilityOne® Award for Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Western region.

Over the past decade, the average SDG&E customer has experienced fewer than one sustained outage a year, while the average amount of time without power from unplanned outages has remained at approximately 70 minutes annually. Momentary interruptions have declined 18% since 2016. In 2025, outage frequency and duration, excluding major event days, were at their lowest levels since 2017.

The results reflect long-term investment in a modern grid, predictive tools that help identify problems earlier and smart-grid technology that can isolate an issue and limit the number of customers affected.

"As we work to improve affordability and deliver energy at the lowest cost possible, safety and reliability will always remain the focus at SDG&E," said Scott Crider, president of SDG&E. "Our customers depend on us to ensure power is there when it's needed most. I'm proud of our employees who work every day to deliver on this commitment and have helped make SDG&E the most reliable utility in the West for 21 years."

Delivering reliable energy around the clock takes more than technology. It takes a skilled local workforce, a resilient supply chain and trusted contractor partnerships. SDG&E's crews live and work in the communities they serve, and they're on call around the clock to maintain the system and restore power quickly. Suppliers and contractors back them up by delivering critical materials when they're needed. Together, they help prevent outages, respond when problems occur and restore power as safely and quickly as possible.

Delivering Reliability More Affordably 
SDG&E also considers cost and efficiency when making the investments that support reliable service. The same technology behind 21 years of top reliability performance, from smart switches that limit outages to AI that helps spot risks sooner, can help the company operate more efficiently and address potential problems before they become larger, more costly repairs.

What 21 Years of Reliability Means for Customers
SDG&E's reliability record rests on investments in people, infrastructure and technology designed to identify risks earlier, limit outages and restore power faster for the 3.6 million people it serves.

  • Seeing Risk Sooner: SDG&E launched Edge Alert Sentinel (EAS), an edge AI collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies and UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography. EAS builds on a network of high-definition cameras and artificial intelligence to support early fire detection. It also works alongside advanced sectionalizing devices that automatically isolate problems on the grid. For customers, that means risks are spotted earlier and fewer homes lose power.
  • A Stronger Grid and Faster Restoration: SDG&E replaced older underground cables and overhead lines, added smart switches that help limit outages, and improved restoration processes to restore power faster. Modernized data systems help teams make quicker decisions and learn from every outage. For customers, that means fewer interruptions, shorter outages, real-time outage updates and an easy-to-use online outage tracking tool.
  • A Culture of Safety: SDG&E was California's first utility to earn Cal/OSHA's elite Voluntary Protection Program safety certification for one of its facilities, exceeding industry standards for operational excellence. For customers, that means a well-trained workforce that keeps safety first while keeping the energy system running.

Independent Oversight, Local Accountability
SDG&E's investments are reviewed by the California Public Utilities Commission through an independent, public process. That oversight helps make sure the work that keeps San Diego's grid among the most reliable in the nation is focused, disciplined and transparent.

"Utilities such as SDG&E are committed to delivering reliable service, enhancing resiliency, and maintaining affordability for their customers," said PA's ReliabilityOne® Program Director Patrick Graves. "Increasingly, technology is being used to augment existing capabilities and improve overall system efficiency. These advancements include more accurate estimated restoration times, the implementation of advanced control systems that allow operators to manage infrastructure through a single user interface, and the integration of hardware and software to streamline restoration efforts. At the same time, utilities are continuing to refine and leverage technology to keep rates affordable and accessible for all customers. At PA, we're proud to be working with utilities that are embracing this kind of innovation to meet evolving customer expectations."

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year PA recognized six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process, which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

Improvements to security, cost, and team experience advance the governed software factory for every enterprise 

  • Agentic remediation helps security teams shrink vulnerability backlogs and prioritize exploitable flaws by real risk.
  • Scheduled automations, now in beta, let GitLab Duo Agent Platform flows handle routine tasks in the background, on a cadence each organization chooses and within the controls it sets.
  • GitLab for Slack, now generally available on GitLab.com, lets teams mention @GitLab in a thread to turn decisions into issues, merge requests, and agent flows.
  • GitLab has made agentic usage on GitLab Duo Agent Platform more efficient, so most customers will see their GitLab Credits go up to twice as far.

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--All Remote - GitLab Inc., the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps, today announced GitLab 19.6, with new capabilities that help security teams work down vulnerability backlogs, make GitLab Credits go further, automate recurring tasks, and bring agents into Slack conversations where teams make decisions. These capabilities help organizations put agents to work across more of the software lifecycle while keeping visibility and control over agent activity and spending.

Engineering, security, and product teams now use agents for a wider range of tasks. As that use grows, organizations need the cost of agent work to stay manageable. They also need automation that lets agents move work forward without someone starting each task. GitLab 19.6 delivers both, with controls that show which agent acted, what it could access, and what it did.

Reducing Vulnerability Backlogs With Agentic Remediation

Every team is adding security findings faster than they can clear them. GitLab 19.6 extends agentic remediation so GitLab Duo security agents can work through more of that backlog. Security managers can turn on agent flows across many projects at once, and teams can run those flows on branches other than the default to fix findings before code merges.

A new vulnerability context flow, in beta for SAST findings, shows whether a flaw is exploitable in practice, so teams can prioritize by exploitability as well as severity. A new mean time to remediation chart shows whether remediation keeps pace with discovery, and group-level policies hold changes with critical or known-exploited vulnerabilities until a designated approver signs off.

When secret detection finds an active GitLab personal access token, teams can now rotate it and fix the code in one step. Rotate and fix, now in beta on GitLab.com, revokes the leaked token, creates a replacement with the same permissions, and stores it in GitLab Secrets Manager. GitLab Duo then opens a merge request that removes the hardcoded token from the code.

Scheduling Recurring Agent Tasks

Recurring tasks such as issue triage wait on a person or an event to start them, so teams complete them late or not at all. Scheduled automations, now in beta, run GitLab Duo Agent Platform flows in the background on a set cadence, from every 15 minutes to every three months. A team can triage new issues daily, or check CI health every hour and post the likely root cause before anyone starts investigating.

Each automation runs as a dedicated service account with scoped permissions, so audit events separate agent activity from human activity and record every change. A redesigned Automations page shows what ran, how often it succeeded, and why a run failed. These controls make scheduled automations a building block of the governed software factory.

Bringing Agents Into Slack Conversations

Software decisions often start in Slack, and someone then retypes them into GitLab. GitLab for Slack lets teams mention @GitLab in a thread or direct message to turn those decisions into issues, merge requests, and agent flows. The agent posts results back to the thread.

Each request runs with the requester's own GitLab permissions, creates an agent session in GitLab, and draws from GitLab Credits. Merge requests follow the same reviews, approvals, and audit trail as any other change.

GitLab for Slack is now generally available on GitLab.com for Premium and Ultimate customers, and GitLab plans to add support for GitLab Self-Managed next month.

Each GitLab Credit Now Does Up to Twice the Work

GitLab has made agentic usage on GitLab Duo Agent Platform more efficient and is passing those savings on to customers. Each task given to Duo Agent Platform now results in fewer model requests, such that most customers will see their GitLab Credits go up to twice as far.

Organizations can use the freed-up credits for the new agentic remediation and scheduled automations, and to extend agentic work to Slack. Customers who have Flex contracts can also use available credits for recently introduced innovations such as GitLab Secrets Manager, Dedicated Hosted Runners, and coming soon, GitLab Orbit. This builds on recent tools for managing credit spend, including impact and cost analytics to track usage and manage credit caps.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Emerita Resources Corp. (TSXV: EMO) (OTCQX: EMOTF) (FSE: LLJA) (the "Company" or "Emerita") presents Executive Chairman letter

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Following my November 16th letter to Emerita shareholders, Mr. Peters issued an immediate rebuttal. He raises numerous accusations and demands yet offers few practical solutions to delivering tangible value for Emerita shareholders. His response also contains statements that misrepresent the Company's position, omit important facts, and oversimplify decisions that require careful judgment.

This type of impulsive response from Mr. Peters is becoming a pattern. His approach to consequential strategic decisions raises concerns about the judgment required to lead a public mining company. Shareholders deserve directors who examine facts, process and consequences before acting.

I will address the points in Mr. Peters' latest response methodically, with facts, and ask the questions his statements leave unanswered.

Emerita's need for capital
Mr. Peters states, "The Company can raise equity capital but we have asked that any shares issued before the meeting do not vote at the meeting" and that "Any strategic investor should have no issue with that".

This statement is not grounded in reality. What investor, especially a sophisticated strategic investor, would invest equity in a company where the outcome and direction of the company is unknown due to a potential fundamental change in the board and significant shift in strategy?

Mr. Peters is free to exercise his rights as a shareholder of the Company, however, the uncertainty created by his requisition and premature attempts to frustrate Emerita's ability to raise capital is one of the reasons for the Board's decision to undertake the strategic review process announced on November 16th.

In addition, we should not speculate what our lender may or may not approve in respect of the Company's credit facility. Mr. Peters' oversimplification of our credit facility should not be interpreted by shareholders as committed immediately available liquidity.

A Strategic Review is an opportunity for shareholders
Mr. Peters has questioned why the strategic review will proceed independently of the requisitioned meeting. The reason is straightforward: protecting shareholder value.

I would ask shareholders to consider another question: What would be gained by preventing the Board from exploring an opportunity that might preserve the option value of their investment?

Emerita's financial and operational obligations continue regardless of the potential proxy contest. The Board cannot suspend its responsibilities because a shareholder wants to hold another vote.

The Board will evaluate potential alternatives. Where a proposed transaction requires shareholder approval, shareholders will decide through the applicable approval process. Mr. Peters should understand that conducting a strategic review for a public company neither deprives shareholders of their rights nor removes the Board's duty to consider opportunities.

Mr. Peters should also understand that a public company conducting a strategic review must respect confidentiality obligations to potential counterparties and applicable disclosure rules. Emerita will update shareholders when legally and commercially appropriate.

Commitment to our Core Business: IBW
Mr. Peters claims to support Emerita's mining business in Spain, yet he offers no concrete plan to advance IBW. He has not identified relevant mining experience of his own. Emerita's current Board includes directors with substantial mining and project experience and fluency in Spanish, including Joseph Belan and Oscar Cabrera and Peter McRae. Mr. Peters should explain what superior capabilities his proposed Board would bring to developing a mining project in Spain.

Mr. Peters says he wants Agne Ahlenius and Joaquin Merino to remain. Mr. Merino is Emerita's Chief Executive Officer and already has the Board's support. Messrs. Merino and Ahlenius have already reiterated their support for your Board.

What the August Meeting was really about
Mr. Peters has mistaken support for change in August as a mandate for his current proposals. He is wrong.

Mr. Peters now describes the August withhold campaign as a vote about who should oversee Falcon. As you know, the campaign centered on whether three longstanding directors should continue to serve on the Board. Your Board respects shareholders' decisions.

The current requisition presents a different question: whether Mr. Peters and his nominees should be given effective control of the Board while the Company faces financing, development and litigation decisions.

Shareholders have told me that the continuing disruption and expense of Mr. Peters' campaign risks making Emerita's already difficult position worse. That concern belongs in the assessment of whether another fight over the Board creates any shareholder value.

Falcon: Where is the Evidence of an alleged Improper Settlement?
Mr. Peters continues to suggest that the Board may rush into an improper settlement of Emerita's Falcon claims. What evidence supports that serious allegation? His suggestion is another example of raising fears about a complex matter without identifying any concrete proposed settlement or an improper Board decision.

The Company has received information from concerned shareholders that Mr. Peters has had at least one discussion with representatives of Lithium Ionic concerning Falcon. Shareholders deserve to know whether anything regarding a potential settlement was discussed by Mr. Peters.

Serious Omissions Raise Questions About Mr. Peter's Agenda — Is There Full Transparency?
As part of our ongoing review of matters related to Mr. Peters and parties close to him, one of the most troubling discrepancies we have identified concerns Mr. Peters' intentions regarding his Board composition.

In the November 3 announcement of his requisition, and as stated on their website, the Concerned Shareholders identified three proposed directors: Andrew Elinesky, Norman Findlay, and Wayne Peters. Yet letters dated November 3 from Mr. Peters' legal counsel to the Ontario Securities Commission and the TSX Venture Exchange describe clear intentions to appoint a fourth individual to the Board: Robin Bienenstock. In other words, shareholders were publicly told about three nominees, while regulators received correspondence confirming Mr. Peters' intention to name four — Ms. Bienenstock is his undisclosed candidate to fill the current vacancy on your Board.

Why did Mr. Peters disclose four directors to regulators while telling shareholders about only three?

Mr. Peters has repeatedly demanded transparency and accountability from Emerita's Board ("Operation Transparency" as he calls it). Shareholders are entitled to expect the same from someone seeking substantial influence over their Company. His public statements and regulatory correspondence should tell the same story. Until he explains the discrepancy, shareholders have reason to question whether they have been given a complete account of his intentions.

Mr. Peters says his group holds only about 5% of the outstanding shares and is therefore a long way from controlling Emerita. His campaign seeks to replace a majority of the Board, and he has included himself as a nominee. If successful, he and his disclosed (and undisclosed) members would collectively exercise effective influence over the Board.

Mr. Peters Has Misrepresented Emerita's Board Appointments Press Release
Mr. Peters cites the September 16 announcement as if it proves departing directors chose their replacements. It does not.

The release thanked Catherine Stretch and Marilia Bento for assisting during the transition. It did not say they voted on their successors. As I confirmed on November 16, the directors who received majority-withhold votes did not participate in the appointment decision.

A statement of thanks is exactly that, and nothing more.

Read the Room
Shareholders are asking why Emerita should endure another disruptive Board contest when qualified directors are already in place, and the Company faces substantial financial, legal and operating challenges. They have told me that they want the Board focused on stabilizing the Company and advancing its assets.

Mr. Peters continues to present himself as the "Voice of Emerita". He is just one (loud) voice, but he does not speak for all Shareholders.

Shareholders I have spoken with tell me his current demands are increasingly out of step with what they want. They supported specific changes in August and recognize that those changes occurred. They now want the Company stabilized and focused on creating value. They are concerned about the consequences of another prolonged fight over the Board.

The Value Equation
Proxy contests ultimately centre on who has a credible strategy to create and realize shareholder value. A list of criticisms and individual proposals is not a strategy. Proposals must fit together and be capable of successful execution.

Mr. Peters has no shortage of lawyers, press releases and online commentators advancing his arguments. Shareholders have heard far less from him about how he would advance IBW and realize value from Falcon. Those are the strategic questions that matter.

The IBW PFS: We Are Providing More Information
Mr. Peters suggests that the Company failed to explain the economics of the IBW Pre-Feasibility Study.

As I acknowledged in my November 16 letter, questions about the PFS and its assumptions are expected in the normal course. Emerita has posted an updated company presentation on its website to address certain questions and explain the development path for IBW. We will provide further clarification where necessary.

An Honest Dialogue with Shareholders
I will continue engaging with shareholders and listening to their concerns. I welcome scrutiny of your Board. I expect shareholders to challenge us, question our decisions and hold us accountable.

I am confident that your Board has the right experience to navigate Emerita's present challenges. We will pursue the strategic review and other credible alternatives for protecting and realizing value for Emerita, its shareholders and stakeholders.

Sincerely,

Joseph Belan

  • Next-generation MRD test with detection sensitivity across major tumor types at 1 part per million or below

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Guardant Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the U.S. clinical launch of Guardant Reveal® Ultra, a new molecular residual disease (MRD) platform for solid tumors offering personalized, ultra-sensitive detection of residual cancer. Built on Guardant’s Smart Platform, Reveal Ultra incorporates tumor-informed, patient-specific genomic alterations to provide one of the most advanced and actionable views of MRD.

Validated on thousands of clinical samples, Guardant Reveal Ultra has demonstrated detection sensitivity of 1 part per million (ppm) or below across major tumor types. The test incorporates patient-specific alterations from thousands of genomic targets spanning all major variant classes, including structural variants. Guardant Reveal Ultra has also been validated with tissue samples containing as little as 5% tumor cellularity, significantly below the typical industry requirement of 20%, enabling testing across a broader range of clinical specimens.

“Reveal Ultra opens a new frontier in MRD detection,” said Helmy Eltoukhy, Guardant Health chairman and co-CEO. “While detecting cancer at one part per million has become an important benchmark, what truly matters is delivering that level of sensitivity reliably across real clinical samples and a broad range of tumor types. Reveal Ultra was built to meet that challenge, bringing extraordinary precision to everyday clinical practice and advancing our ability to track and manage each patient’s cancer throughout their journey.”

Guardant Reveal Ultra is designed as a connected experience, enabling physicians the option of a direct path from MRD detection to clinical action through Guardant360® Liquid. Together with Guardant Reveal®’s best-in-class tissue-free MRD detection and therapy monitoring capabilities, and Guardant360 Liquid and Guardant360® Tissue for comprehensive genomic profiling, Guardant Reveal Ultra completes Guardant’s precision oncology portfolio. These solutions work hand-in-hand to support physicians in selecting therapies, monitoring treatment response, detecting residual disease, and managing cancer throughout the patient journey.

About Guardant Health

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. Key Terms

molecular residual diseasemedical
Molecular residual disease is the tiny amount of cancer that can remain in the body after treatment and is detectable only by sensitive tests that find cancer DNA or other molecular traces. It matters to investors because these measurements can predict relapse, guide whether additional therapy is needed, and shape the market for diagnostics and drugs—much like finding embers after a fire helps decide if more firefighting is required.
structural variantstechnical
Structural variants are large-scale changes in an organism’s DNA—such as missing, extra, flipped, or rearranged chunks of genetic material—that are like tearing out, duplicating, or reshuffling chapters in a book. Investors should care because these changes can drive or explain diseases, alter how well diagnostics and therapies work, and shift the commercial and regulatory outlook for drugs, tests, and gene-based treatments.
tumor cellularitymedical
The proportion of a tissue sample that is made up of actual tumor (malignant) cells rather than non-malignant components such as stroma, inflammatory cells, blood, or necrotic debris; expressed as a percentage of tumor cells among the nucleated cells in the specimen. Tumor cellularity is assessed by a pathologist on the biopsy or surgical specimen and affects how reliable molecular tests (like DNA sequencing or biomarker assays) are because low cellularity can dilute tumor-derived signals; it can also vary within and between samples due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling or processing factors.
